newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid workers tell of fierce battle for Zaire city.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers tell of fierce battle for Zaire city.

text.p: Aid workers evacuated from the war-ravaged east Zaire city of Goma said on Saturday they had been in the middle of pitched battles, lying flat on the floor of their offices.
They said the fiercest fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels backed by Rwandan soldiers was on Friday.

"At one o'clock in the afternoon we started to hear firing not far from the house we were in. By 1.15 the firing was really close," said Michelle Quintaglie of the U.N. World Food Programme. "After that there were 50 aid workers flat on the floor for an hour-and-a-half."
"We saw three Zairean soldier dead on the front lawn," she said, adding: "There was actually fighting in our backyard. It was by far the most dramatic situation I have ever been in."
On Saturday more than 100 international aid workers made a five-minute dash by car for the Rwandan border town of Gisenyi.
They were unharmed during the fighting but their vehicles bore the scars of earlier battles.

"The car I drove out in now has six bullet holes in it," said Quintaglie. "The biggest problem is that we have left behind us hundreds of thousands of refugees who have absolutely nobody to feed them."

The situation in Goma itself remained confused on Saturday. I entered the city behind Rwandan troops fighting on the side of Tutsi rebels and saw no Zairean troops in the part of the city I was able to enter.
Journalists managed to reach a crossroads outside the U.N. building before being forced to turn back under heavy incoming and outgoing machinegun fire.
One western diplomat in Gisenyi told Reuters: "We are hearing that the Zairean army are completely pulling out of Goma but that they will have one last go at shelling Gisenyi before they leave.
It was not clear who was in charge of Goma airport.
